The expansive library of sci-fi shows is ever-growing, but what has already been brought to TV screens deserves to be acknowledged, especially the series that are incredibly fun to watch. Those extremely fun sci-fi gems use strange futures, aliens, space travel, alternate worlds, advanced technology, and impossible ideas to create plots packed full of humor, adventure, danger, personality, and style.

Entertaining sci-fi shows like the action-packed cyberpunk adventure Altered Carbon and the cult classic Firefly, which turns space travel into a scrappy outlaw adventure full of sharp banter, found family, humor, and charm, are just two series in the genre that genuinely feel fun and exciting, without ever feeling distant. Compiled on this list are nine of the most fun sci-fi shows of all time that offer viewers genuinely entertaining worlds to escape into.

blocks.c: The cast of Misfits in a locker room in Season 2

blocks.x: This underrated British sci-fi series is a hilariously great time that takes superpowers and somehow makes them chaotic, messy, rude, and completely unpredictable. Misfits follows a group of teenage offenders who gain strange and unique abilities during a freak lightning storm and immediately prove that they are not at all prepared for the intense responsibility.

Misfits wields a reckless energy with a captivating appeal that stems from just how wild and genuinely funny the show gets while keeping up with its sharp sci-fi ideas. The show takes time travel, powers, immortality, body swapping, and other entertaining tropes in the genre and turns them into a complete disaster caused by individuals who barely know how to handle normal life. But what truly makes Misfits a hypnotic good time is its strange ability to feel both dangerous and laugh-out-loud funny, while delivering chaos most shows could only dream of.

blocks.c: Bender with his eyes zoomed in at a bar with Leela and Fry in Futurama.

blocks.x: Futurama is one of the finest sci-fi series of all time simply because it uses its science fiction as playfully as possible. The series centers around pizza delivery boy Fry (Billy West), who awakens 1000 years in the future after accidentally falling into a freezer on the job, only to join another, more adventurous delivery service, which hosts a crew of truly odd employees.

Futurama is no doubt one of the most entertaining sci-fi shows ever to exist, because it delivers ideas of the sci-fi genre as truly clever, hilariously silly, and weirdly heartfelt. From robots, time travel, and aliens to parallel universes, space delivery routes, and memorable characters, the show does an amazing job of being continuously fun and creative, all without ever losing its surprising amounts of genuine warmth. Futurama is absurd, often chaotic, and honestly some of the best fun ever brought to sci-fi television, which helps explain how it has lasted for as long as it has while receiving constant praise for being an all-time animated favorite.

blocks.c: Two characters stand in a corridor and look ahead with serious expressions in Farscape.

blocks.x: This sci-fi watch is the oldest on this list and stands as one of the most fun and bizarre shows to ever make it onto TV. Farscape focuses on astronaut John Crichton (Ben Browder), who finds himself in the far corners of the universe after a space trial goes horribly wrong. Now aboard a living ship with a fugitive crew, John must navigate aliens, strange cultures, enemies, and constant danger.

Farscape is definitely not the most popular on this list — in fact, as a whole, the series is incredibly underrated — but very few shows embrace their cosmic weirdness as fully as the captivating series does. It's a fun space adventure story that never feels like a safe or generic space TV show. With big emotions, strange aliens, and storytelling that often takes the turn no one expects, Farscape stands as a bold and extremely fun sci-fi standout that deserves far more attention than it's received.

blocks.c: Joel Kinnaman readies himself to do drugs in a neon-lit alley in Netflix's 'Altered Carbon'

blocks.x: While Altered Carbon’s second and last season definitely had mixed reviews, the series still claims a spot as one of the most entertaining additions to the sci-fi genre, especially because of its amazing initial season. Set in a future where human consciousness can be stored and moved between bodies, the series follows the former soldier Takeshi Kovacs (Joel Kinnaman), who is brought back in a new body centuries after his death and hired by wealthy businessman Laurens Bancroft (James Purefoy) to solve Bancroft’s own mysterious murder.

Altered Carbon is one of the darkest sci-fi watches on this list, but the show still stands as one of the most fun to come from the genre because of its wild ideas and awesome style. The Netflix series is slick and pulpy, an entertaining mixture of body-swapping tropes, mystery, futuristic tech, brutal action, and a very noir atmosphere, which makes it one of the most captivating cyberpunk worlds seen on TV. Altered Carbon is a standout series that may be a bit heavy, but is definitely never dull.

blocks.c: A scared Will Byers in 'Stranger Things' Season 1.

blocks.x: This Netflix sci-fi icon masterfully combines supernatural danger with friendship, nostalgia, mystery, and thrilling coming-of-age adventure. Set in the town of Hawkins, Indiana, Stranger Things centers on a group of friends after the disappearance of Will Byers (Noah Schnapp), a strange event that leads them right to a mysterious girl with powerful abilities and tons of secrets.

Stranger Things’ fun comes from the way it transforms scary sci-fi moments into a huge emotional adventure built around lovable characters. The series brilliantly captures the joy of the genre’s most entertaining adventure. From psychic powers, teen romances, and alternate dimensions to loyal friends, monsters, and government labs, the series is a mixed bag of highly entertaining content. Stranger Things is an extremely fun sci-fi gem not only because it's excitingly thrilling, but because it’s an easy binge with genuine emotion and rewatchable moments of kid-like adventure.

blocks.c: Alan Tudyk as Harry sitting behind his desk in Resident Alien.

blocks.x: Resident Alien stands as one of the most fun sci-fi series ever brought to television because it takes an alien invasion premise and turns it into an entertaining and quite hilarious small-town comedy. The series focuses on an alien who crashes onto Earth, finding himself in the small town of Patience, Colorado, where he assumes the identity of local doctor Harry Vanderspeigle (Alan Tudyk), slowly becoming entangled in the very human lives of the town’s residents.

Resident Alien is strange, but also weirdly charming. It blends murder mystery, small-town drama, alien mission, and awkward comedy into a story that is genuinely funny because the main character understands next to nothing about being an everyday human being. Resident Alien wields an addictive and highly entertaining story, all without constant explosions and outlandish spectacle, marking it as one of the most fun sci-fi shows ever created.

blocks.c: Rick and MOrty fighting each other in Rick and Morty Season 9.

blocks.x: This chaotic animated sci-fi series is one of the biggest hits in the genre and stands strong as an extremely fun viewing experience. Rick and Morty centers around the extremely reckless, alcoholic genius, Rick (Ian Cardoni), and his constantly anxious grandson, Morty (Harry Belden), as they travel across dimensions, timelines, planets, and realities.

Rick and Morty is easily one of the most fun sci-fi shows to ever exist simply because it treats the multiverse like an endless joke machine and a source of existential panic. The series pushes sci-fi absurdity, and it pushes it pretty far. Rick and Morty makes science fiction feel truly limitless and incredibly unpredictable. It’s a hilariously fun sci-fi watch that uses portals, alien civilizations, clones, simulations, and cosmic threats to create consistently comedic situations that range from violent and strange to funny and much darker than one would have expected while watching the show.

blocks.c: The crew of Firefly prepares for battle.

blocks.x: Firefly is one of the few short-lived sci-fi shows to have left behind such constant affection and lasting devotion from fans despite its very brief run. The series focuses on the crew of Serenity as they dodge danger, take on jobs, argue like family, and survive on the edges of a future society.

Firefly wields an exceptional charm that comes mainly from its entertaining blend of humor, action, space western energy, and characters that almost instantly feel incredibly lovable. It's a perfect fit for this list of fun sci-fi masterpieces because it’s a series rife with adventure and personality. With exciting missions, jokes, and friendships that feel genuinely familial, Firefly is a lasting sci-fi classic that earns its status and praise as one of the most captivating and enticingly fun adventures that fans still talk about.

This modern sci-fi gem is as chaotic as it is extremely fun. Based on the video game series, Fallout follows the sheltered young woman Lucy MacLean (Ella Purnell), who abandons the safety of her underground Vault to venture out into the dangerous post-apocalyptic wasteland of Los Angeles in search of her kidnapped father.

Fallout is one of the greatest additions to the sci-fi genre. Viewers find themselves on a wild ride through its bizarre post-apocalyptic world, where dark comedy, brutal violence, strange creatures, futuristic tech, and wildly unpredictable characters work somehow seamlessly together. What truly makes Fallout such a standout watch is the captivating way that its world is both laugh-out-loud hilarious and grotesquely horrifying, marking it as a well-balanced sci-fi gem with a unique spark.
